name: Question 3
problem:
$$
x=\,\,b
$$

Let $A=QR$  be a QR decomposition of an $m\times n$ matrix $A$ with linearly independent columns, and the expression above gives the least-squares solution of $Ax=b.$ From left to right, what are the missing parts of the equation?
worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the normal equation

$$
{A}^{T}Ax={A}^{T}b.
$$

Substituting $A=QR,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}Ax & ={A}^{T}b \\ (QR)^{T}QRx & =(QR)^{T}b \\ {R}^{T}({Q}^{T}Q)Rx & ={R}^{T}{Q}^{T}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Q$ has orthonormal columns, ${Q}^{T}Q=I,$ and we get

$$
{R}^{T}Rx={R}^{T}\,{Q}^{T}b.
$$

Then, since ${R}^{T}$ is invertible, pre-multiplying by $({R}^{T})^{-1}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}({R}^{T})^{-1}\cdot {R}^{T}Rx & =({R}^{T})^{-1}\cdot {R}^{T}{Q}^{T}b \\ Rx & ={Q}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $R$ is invertible, pre-multiplying by ${R}^{-1}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}^{-1}\cdot Rx & ={R}^{-1}\cdot {Q}^{T}b \\ x & =\,\,\,{R}^{-1}\,\,{Q}^{T}\,b.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing parts of the equation are ${R}^{-1}$ and ${Q}^{T}.$

html:
Question 3
?

x=AAb

Let A=QR be a QR decomposition of an m×n matrix A with linearly independent columns, and the expression above gives the least-squares solution of Ax=b. From left to right, what are the missing parts of the equation?

a
R−1 and Q
b
R−1 and QT
c
Q and R−1
d
R and QT
e
Q and R
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The least-squares solution of Ax=b satisfies the normal equation

ATAx=ATb.

Substituting A=QR, we obtain

ATAx=ATb(QR)TQRx=(QR)TbRT(QTQ)Rx=RTQTb.

Since Q has orthonormal columns, QTQ=I, and we get

RTRx=RTQTb.

Then, since RT is invertible, pre-multiplying by (RT)−1 gives

(RT)−1⋅RTRx=(RT)−1⋅RTQTbRx=QTb

Finally, since R is invertible, pre-multiplying by R−1 gives

R−1⋅Rx=R−1⋅QTbx=|R−1QTb.

Therefore, the missing parts of the equation are R−1 and QT.
